summary: Obfuscated code execution channel via XOR-decoded payload in package.json metadata
details: On require, index.js reads a numeric byte array from a non-standard `_b` field in package.json, XORs each byte with 0x96, and passes the result to the Function constructor along with `require` and `__dirname`. In version 1.0.1 the decoded bytes resolve to a trivial `console.log(1)`, but the package exports an empty object and advertises itself as a utility, so the only functional behavior shipped is this dynamic-execution channel. The payload is stored in a manifest field under a single-letter key, outside any shipped.js source, and is only reachable through the XOR transform — a deliberate obfuscation shape that lets any future published version execute arbitrary author-controlled code at import time with full access to `require` and the installing project's directory.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
